title: emit-stage-handoff-corpus
content:
Purpose:
Capture a small, human-curated corpus of end-to-end traces that highlight emission-stage handoffs and stage-boundary delays. Goal is to identify repeatable p95/p99 behaviors that are not visible in aggregate stage charts and to produce a small reproducible test set for microbenchmarks and regressions.

Context / why this is different: 
- We already have broad latency catalogs and cohort studies. This doc focuses on the specific handoff between the token-generation emitter and downstream egress/egress-io, plus upstream kernel transitions (attn->kv->emit) where subtle serialization/lock contention shows up.
- Looking for microburst signatures where the emitter waits (spin or block) for resources that are externally visible as p95/p99 spikes but only in a narrow seqlen or coldstart cohort.

Data set & selection criteria: 
- Time window: 2025-01-10 -> 2025-02-28 production traces sampled at 5x for tail events.
- Trace filters: responses with total latency > 1200ms, and final token count >= 32; include both coldstart (host warm=0) and warm host events.
- Cohorts: short (<=64 tokens), medium (65-256), long (257-1024).
- Kept top 120 traces after dedup by request hash; prioritized traces with >2 stage reschedules or >1 cross-host handoff.

Methodology / instrumentation notes: 
- Instrumentation tags: emitter.enter/exit, kv.fetch.start/end, attn-kernel.start/end, batch-assemble.start/end, egress.write.start/end, net-egress.wait.
- Wall-clock measured at stage boundaries; we also collect CPU desched counts and epoll wait durations for the egress socket.
- Sampled memstats and GPU kernel queue depth at trace start/emit boundary (best-effort).

Summary metrics (corpus aggregate):
- Cohort short (n=42): p50=220ms, p95=740ms, p99=1,220ms
- Cohort medium (n=48): p50=420ms, p95=1,180ms, p99=2,400ms
- Cohort long (n=30): p50=1,100ms, p95=2,940ms, p99=6,800ms
- Coldstart subset (n=34 overall): median uplift ~+320ms, p95 uplift ~+1,100ms

Per-stage median fraction (across corpus):
- Tokenize/parse: 6%
- Encode/initial KV: 14%
- Attention kernels: 38%
- KV fetch & cache misses: 8%
- Emit (tokenization->emit loop): 22%
- Egress write / network: 9%
- Other scheduling/wait: 3%

Tail signatures observed (p95/p99 hotspots):
1) Emitter spin-loop handoff: 
   - Symptom: rapid alternation of emit.enter/emit.exit with <1ms kernel runtimes but >300ms wall-clock between successive emits.
   - Correlates with: high epoll wait on the egress FD and context-switch counts on the worker thread.
   - Hypothesis: backpressure on egress path causes emitter to relinquish CPU; when it resumes, it suffers micro-serialization at the per-request mutex.

2) KV-fetch serialization at high seqlen: 
   - Symptom: bursts of sequential kv.fetch.start that serialize across tokens causing O(n) behavior for long sequences.
   - Correlates with: increased RPC latency to local KV store / GPU-side memcopy stalls.
   - Hypothesis: cache-miss path allocates buffers while holding a global lock.

3) Kernel queue preemption: 
   - Symptom: attn-kernel.start delayed with GPU queue depth high and CPU scheduling latency elevated.
   - Correlates with: machine-level maintenance job or background host activity.
   - Hypothesis: noisy-neighbor containers (esp. on Dedicated nodes) can push kernel start beyond soft SLO windows.

Representative trace excerpts (IDs and notes):
- trace-20250118-1a2b: medium cohort, p99-path; emitter shows 520ms of idle between emits; egress epoll wait spikes coincide. (see JIRA-2387)
- trace-20250202-4f7c: long cohort, KV-miss storm; repeated buffer allocations at kv.fetch path, memcopy stalls recorded.
- trace-20250130-9d01: coldstart case, host warm=0; GPU warmup + emitter handoff multiplies p95 latency.

Quick sampling of stage breakdowns from three exemplar traces (numbers in ms):
- T(trace-20250118-1a2b): tokenize 18, encode 62, attn kernels 210, kv 28, emit loop 520 (idle sacks), egress 24, total 862
- T(trace-20250202-4f7c): tokenize 36, encode 110, attn kernels 840, kv 480 (misses/serial), emit 152, egress 30, total 1,648
- T(trace-20250130-9d01): tokenize 12, encode 48, attn kernels 420, kv 96, emit 320 (cold path), egress 34, total 930

Hypotheses and quick checks: 
- H1: Egress backpressure causes emitter to drop CPU slice and re-enter in batches -> reproduce by throttling egress device with tc/netem on a staging node; expect per-token emission spacing to increase and p95 to rise.
- H2: KV-miss path holds coarse lock during buffer allocation -> simulate with synthetic workload that triggers cache misses and measure lock hold times (perf trace or lockwatch).
- H3: Background host jobs cause GPU kernel preemption -> run with node-isolation (cpuset + gpu exclusivity) to check tail reduction.

Short experiments to run (priority order):
- EXP-A: Repeat trace-20250118 scenario on staging by replaying the request with egress throttle at 50% and capture traces. (owner: Ethan)
- EXP-B: Add micro-profiling to kv.fetch for allocation path and add histograms for allocation-time-per-fetch. (owner: Mariana)
- EXP-C: Run a dedicated node with no other containers and a pinned CPU/GPU set; replay long-cohort traces for 24h to measure tail drift. (owner: Jonas)

Action items / next steps: 
- Create small microbench harness that reproduces emitter->egress backpressure (due: 2025-03-09, owner: Ethan).
- Open a short-term lock refactor spike for kv.fetch allocation (link PR draft: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/512).
- Add a tail-check guard in prod overlays: if emit idle > 200ms across >4 tokens, mark trace and route to low-priority worker pool for diagnosis.

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts: 
- Might be useful to compute per-trace "emit inter-token jitter" distribution (stddev of inter-emit gaps) and correlate with p99.
- Consider exposing an internal CLI to replay single trace with exact timing to staging nodes (will make debugging deterministic).

References: 
- JIRA-2387: emitter tailcase investigation (link above)
- PR: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/512 (kv allocation instrumentation)

Raw trace ids (kept for offline analysis):
["trace-20250118-1a2b","trace-20250120-8c3d","trace-20250123-6b6f","trace-20250202-4f7c","trace-20250130-9d01","trace-20250214-0e5a"]

If you pick this up: start with EXP-A and post results in #eng-serving-runtime with the trace screenshots and flamegraphs. Ping me (Priya) if you need a quick pairing on trace selection.
